display.title: Episode 438: The Dike (Tisha B'Av)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's Tisha B'Av show: Torah, avodah and kindness as a diet for the soul, the story of a lost girl brought home by Shabbos candles, and the ancient tune of Eichah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Tisha B'Av 5750. Uncle Yossi explains that the world stands on three things: learning Torah, our lifeline; davening, since, as the Rambam taught, only Hashem can grant what we need; and acts of kindness, above all tzedakah, which refines the giver. Together they are Hashem's prescribed diet for a healthy neshamah. A first-grade boy recites the Shema in Studio 604, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time, 'The Dike', is set in a Dutch town by the sea. Two devoted sisters are in school when the dike breaks; seven-year-old Gittel, whose old injury reopens, falls behind and is carried off by a harsh old woman who tells her she has no family left and works her hard for three years until she forgets how to keep Shabbos. Sent alone to a distant fair, she sees Shabbos candles in a window on her way back, remembers her home, knocks, and finds her own family. Uncle Yossi then speaks about music as Hashem's gift and introduces the ancient tune of Eichah sung on Tisha B'Av, praying that this will be the last Tisha B'Av in golus. The show ends with candle-lighting times and a sponsor.
display.lesson: The light of the Shabbos candles can bring a lost Jewish child back home; Torah, davening and kindness keep the soul healthy.

date.note: 'This Tisha B'Av'; candle time 7:51 PM fits Fri 3 Aug 1990; catalog topic '10 Av, Eichah' = Tuesday night after the fast.

advisories.note: A dike breaks and a town flees the flood; a girl is left behind asleep as the water rises.
A harsh old woman keeps a lost girl for three years, tells her she has no family, overworks her and threatens a beating.
Tisha B'Av and the songs of exile.
